claims.text: Corrosion resistance in steels for chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications is governed by a chromium-enriched passive oxide film.
The chromium-enriched passive film dynamically self-repairs and remains protective under high temperature, corrosive media, and moderate irradiation.
The proposed temperature, media, and low-to-moderate radiation levels are representative of chemical-processing and nuclear-power operating conditions.
Preferential oxidation of chromium and other alloying elements forms the protective passive film.
A dense oxide barrier impedes further metal dissolution and improves corrosion resistance.
Localized breakdowns of the passive film under combined thermal, chemical, and irradiation stresses are rapidly repaired.
Rapid passive-film repair maintains a stable, low corrosion rate.
Excessive radiation flux can cause irreversible film thickening or breakdown and thereby compromise corrosion resistance.
Under the specified conditions, steel possessing the proposed dynamic-film mechanism will have lower corrosion current density than the selected baselines.
After minor disruption, the chromium-rich passive film will reform rapidly.
The dynamically repaired film will produce minimal changes in impedance over time.
Surface oxides can evolve from initially unstable growth toward a steady state in molten chloride salt at 450–650 °C.
The proposed self-healing chromium-film mechanism holds throughout the 450–650 °C range in the specified processing fluids or simulated reactor primary water under moderate irradiation.
Extremely high radiation fluxes or radically different chemical environments may prevent the proposed mechanism from operating.
The interplay between radiation-induced defects and oxide-regeneration kinetics is not fully quantified.
The radiation-flux threshold separating self-healing from detrimental film disruption is unknown.
Capacitive EIS behavior and high impedance are signatures of a compact passive oxide film.
Corrosion current density obtained from polarization measurements provides a quantitative indicator of dissolution rate and corrosion resistance.
